notes.title: A peek at the upcoming Update + Autumn Sale!
notes.notes: [p]Hi everyone! [/p][p]Thank you for your continued support of Let Them Trade! We're so very happy to see you having fun with the game and getting your feedback here and on our discord <3[/p][p][/p][p]The team is back in their groove and working tirelessly to bring you a new update soon - so today we wanted to share a little snippet of what you can expect when it drops![/p][p][/p][p][b]New resources and research tree changes![/b][/p][p]We are reworking the research tree and the production chains. New resources got added to make the middle to late game more interesting. Accompaning that are new buildings and icons for the new resources.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Visual variety![/b][/p][p]We're introducing tile variations for some tile types, like different forests.[/p][p][/p][p][b]New Bounty System![/b][/p][p]Cities will place a bounty on the bandits who stole their goods. Players will be able to collect the bounty after capturing the bandit.[/p][p]Also a lot of smaller improvements in regards to the bandits.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Smarter Transporters![/b][/p][p]Inner-city transporters will be able to work more efficiently. They are able to transport multiple resources and do multiple tasks at once. They try to combine different routes for different resources and to avoid travelling empty when there is something on their way they can pick up. They also prioritize the resources they need to transport differently. And loading/unloading times are now influenced by how much they carry. (that was a fixed time till now) The UI now reflects how much a transporter is transporting.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Performance optimisations![/b][/p][p]Reworking our rendering to be much more stable and produce less visual artifacts. Lower-end systems should get more frames now and everyone should experience less crashes.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Balancing![/b][/p][p]Rebalanced the economy[/p][p]Added new modifications[/p][p]Increased input and output capacities[/p][p][/p][p][b]Quality-of-life changes![/b][/p][p]Redid the general resource overview in the top left to be much clearer[/p][p]Quickly access "donate" and "collect" buttons by pressing and holding the "Shift" key[/p][p]Lots of smaller bug fixes and tweaks[/p][p][/p][p]We'll post a more detailed changelog once the update is out![/p][p]Until then, owners of Let Them Trade can hop on the Discord to try out some of the new changes now![/p][p][/p][p]One more thing - Let Them Trade will participate in [b]Steam Autumn Sale[/b] next week, so if you're looking to get the game with a nice discount now's your chance![/p][p][/p][p]See you soon and happy trading![/p]

notes.title: Cozy new city builder Let Them Trade feels like Civilization 7 with less stress
notes.notes:
Trading is one of those magical problem solvers in city-building games. Whether it's securing that valuable resource you need to support a unit's production in Civilization 7, or offloading supplies you don't need to secure those you do in Simcity. Indie studio Spaceflower's new game Let Them Trade embraces this fully, setting you on a course to build out an ever-expanding network of cities that can exchange their resources. It's a relaxing blend of managing settlements and optimizing your production lines, and it's out now.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: News: We have a release date!
notes.notes:
[h2]Release Date[/h2]

Yes, finally! We have a release date for Let Them Trade. The long wait will be over on the:

[b]24th of July, 2025[/b] 

This is when Let Them Trade will release fully. It only took us 6 years to get to this point, but here it is. 

If you played the demo you can expect a lot of new & exciting stuff in the full release, like: 
[list]
[*]The higher tiers of the research tree with new resources and production chains, 
[*]A campaign mode with varied scenarios for you to play 
[*]Bandits and the possibility to shush them away with your knight and their entourage 
[*]A map editor and the option to share your maps with the community via the Steam workshop.
[/list]

[h2]Steam Next Fest[/h2]

Thank you all for the amazing response to our demo so far! We are really glad you enjoy what we showed you so far.

If you like our demo, make sure you don't miss our [b]Steam Next Fest[/b] update! This update will bring you a first look into our bandit system and bring a new use to the knights. We are really excited for your feedback on that! The update will go live on June 9th, in time with the Steam Next Fest. It will be served as an update to the regular demo.

In the meantime, if you want to stay updated and chat with our community, please [url=https://discord.gg/5EueZC8]join our Discord[/url]! :)

Sincerely,
Spaceflower

notes.title: News: The demo for Let Them Trade is out now!
notes.notes:
It's been a long way, but the time is finally here and we are happy to share the first public demo of our game Let Them Trade with you!

Since the start of the development the game went through many phases: An analogue prototype, a concept version, the first prototype in Unity, the first version in Unreal... And many more. Many versions and features were scrapped in favor of refining the game's design into something that is equally fun, understandable but still fits with the very core values of Let Them Trade. 

But now, 6 years after the initial start of the project, we are finally able to show you a version of the game of which we can say "This is something we are proud of." and "This is something people will enjoy".

So, without further ado, you can play the demo here:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3465460/Let_Them_Trade_Demo/

If you like to keep in touch with the ongoing development of Let Them Trade, feel free to join [url=https://discord.com/invite/yaTeefS]our Discord[/url]. This also where you can leave feedback regarding the demo. And if you liked it, please leave a positive review on Steam, it helps a lot. :)

Also a big thank you to all our playtesters, who eagerly tested early versions of this demo and gave us a lot of valuable feedback. Thank you all so much <3

Have fun playing!

Sincerely,
Spaceflower

notes.title: Dev-Diary: Recording our title track with a real orchestra (Video)
notes.notes:
Our composer Max went to a very unique event where a bunch of indie studios got together for the chance of recording a piece of their soundtrack with an orchestra. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37853833/253118ef27c777ca1101de7a9cfb347384166943.jpg[/img]
[i]Our composer Max and our developer Amadeus in the recording studios of the German Film Orchestra Babelsberg. [/i]

Usually, recording your game's soundtrack with a real orchestra is too expensive for a smaller indie studio like us to handle. That's why most composers and producers use sample libraries nowadays, where they get the sound of the real instruments recorded in multiple different variations and are then able to arrange them to their liking, all without the overhead of a real orchestra. 

But having human musicians perform your music piece is still something different. The way they can articulate musical phrases, the many subtleties in their playing, the interaction between the different instrument groups and the special character of the room and the situation - that is something that is really hard to reproduce digitally. A piece recorded by a bunch of professionals will almost always sound better than one produced in your bedroom.

[h1]The event: Live Score Berlin[/h1]

But how can a studio like Spaceflower afford to do this? This is where the guys over at [url=https://www.audiocreatures.com/]AudioCreatures[/url] come in! They had the great idea to just book an orchestra for a whole day and then splitting this day up into multiple slots where different game studios could get the chance to have a piece of their game's soundtrack recorded. And that was the event "Live Score Berlin"

So our composer Max and our developer Amadeus headed over to Potsdam, to get our title track recorded by the "German Film Orchestra Babelsberg". They captured their thoughts and impressions in a series of videos which we cut together as some sort of mini-VLOG. Max also explains the challenges when you have to translate digitally produced music into music that's played by real people. 

You can find the YouTube video below. We originally created the video with the intention of posting it on TikTok (which we also did), so desktop readers, please bring your monitors into an upright position before continuing on to watch the video! 

[previewyoutube=WvqOZPYTrYY;full][/previewyoutube]

I think the track turned out great. What do you think, should we release the full track outside of the game as well? 

Sincerely,
Spaceflower

notes.title: Dev-Diary: Work continues on Let Them Trade
notes.notes:
Updates may have become a bit sparse, but we have not stopped working on Let Them Trade! We will try to keep you more updated from now on, but only time will tell if we can manage. :)

Anyway, here is a small recap of what has happened since the last update:

[h1]We went to Gamescom! [/h1]

If you have seen our last announcement post, you will know that we made a trip to Gamescom! If you don't know, Gamescom is a large games exhibition happening each year in Cologne, Germany. If I'm not mistaken, it is the biggest gaming exhibition in the world. 

Our developer Amadeus and our composer Max went there to represent Spaceflower and show Let Them Trade at the booth of ByteRockers' Games. 

Their feedback: Manning the booth for several days was very exhausting, but at the same time it was very fun and exciting to get the game into the hands of the players. Thank you to everyone who came by and gave the game a try!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37853833/081f96f1fde67f534334b10247fa75c351b25386.jpg[/img]

[h1]We started our first (semi) public playtest![/h1]

Inspired by the feedback we got at Gamescom, we started handing out the game to even more players. We started our first [b]Community Playtest[/b] with our loyal Discord members who waited patiently for quite some time. The playtest is still ongoing, but we already got a lot of valuable feedback! 

Between a lot of bugs and still poorly-balanced features, we got a lot of positive feedback for the game, which we are of course very happy about! 

If you would like to take part in a future playtest, make sure to join our [url=https://discordapp.com/invite/yaTeefS]Discord[/url]! We will inform you there if it's time to do another one. 

In the meantime, check out this huge and amazing map one of our playtesters made with our integrated map-editor:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37853833/58eb7cc9a02310ad6d4eb738799bdfecae0edae5.jpg[/img]


[h1]We worked hard on the game![/h1]

You wouldn't believe it, we actually worked on the game as well! 

Actually, that's where most of our time went and that's also why we haven't released a development-update in quite some time. Some things took some figuring out and many things were rebuilt. And while doing that, we most often keep to ourselves, but we are slowly figuring out that working closely with the community helps us figuring out whats best for the game a lot quicker. 

We will tell you more in our coming entries of our dev-diary! So make sure to follow the game and keep an eye out for new posts here on Steam! 

But for now, have some scribbles:

Spaceflower

notes.title: Dev-Diary: Trader Models and Pathfinding
notes.notes:
[h1]We've thrown out another placeholder![/h1]
The next placeholder had to go and was kicked out, this time it was [b]the trader's[/b].
We replaced the flying "somethings" with an actual model of how the traders are supposed to look in the game - a carriage with brave horsies in front of it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37853833/58d6b0a310631256cc64f881bf68719393af43d7.png[/img]

They also rotate into the proper direction, so they'll see and be able to avoid any obstacles in their way.

Speaking of obstacles:

[h1]Base Pathfinding Implementation[/h1]

We also have a working pathfinding implementation now.
What is that and what does this mean, you ask?

It's the ability of the game to find a decent way from one hexagonal tile of the map to any other - including accounting for hard to pass terrain or not all passable fields.

Check out this example, where the game found a neat way from the left to the right end of this road while avoiding and "walking around" the impassable mountains:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37853833/bf08dba294f1801f10739e409dec607f16f186c4.png[/img]


So yah, all in all, we're coming along nicely,
stay tuned for more updates - and the closed Early Alpha soon!

[i][b]-Your Spaceflower Team[/b][/i]

notes.title: Dev-Diary: The First Milestone has been Reached!
notes.notes:
[h1][b]MILESTONE 1[/b] - we have a "game loop"[/h1]

[b]Ladies and gentle men, we're so super happy to tell you that [i]Let Them Trade[/i] is making good progress![/b]

It has been a bit quiet since we started working on the prototype of [i]Let Then Trade[/i], lot's of work needed to be (re)done as we had to start from scratch and do everything new, since we switched to Unreal Engine 4.

But we're finally on track again, and from now on we don't want to leave the fast lane.

[h2]The First Milestone is here[/h2]

Our first, big goal was to get a "complete game loop" that also looks nice.
What does this mean?
This means that at this stage, the game is basically running and things are already happening!

Thomas has worked his incredible magic and created fantastic new assets (the game tiles and everything on them), Michael ("Hellcat") cast some dark voodoo to fill the traders, that are already existing in the game, with enough life so they can make profit yielding decisions on what resource to buy at which city and where to sell it again and last but not least, Alex and Flo joined forces for the first bit of UI!

[url=https://twitter.com/therealhellcat/status/1307288285279068160][img]https://secure.hellcat.net/spflltt/lttms1scshsat480.gif[/img][/url]

So yeah, big progress in the houses of [i]Let Them Trade[/i].

And be asured, we're already having a detailed plan on how to get to the next milestones - we will, of course, keep you very updated, so you always know what's up :-)

If you feel like you want more updates, or even give feedback and suggestions - or just want to chat with us a bit - follow us on the Tweeter and/or join our Discord:

Discord => https://discordapp.com/invite/yaTeefS

Cheers!
